questions.stem: Which digit can NEVER be the units digit of a perfect square? (a) 1 (b) 4 (c) 7 (d) 9
Explain in one line why 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25 is not a coincidence.
questions.answer: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n²; here n = 5, so the sum is 5² = 25.
questions.markingKey: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n²; here n = 5, so the sum is 5² = 25.

questions.stem: A student says: 'A number ending in 6 is always a perfect square, because 16 and 36 are.' Give a counter-example and explain what the units-digit rule really tells us.
questions.answer: 26 ends in 6 but lies between 25 and 36, so it is not a square. The units-digit rule only rules numbers OUT (ending in 2, 3, 7, 8); it never proves a number IS a square.
questions.markingKey: 26 ends in 6 but lies between 25 and 36, so it is not a square. The units-digit rule only rules numbers OUT (ending in 2, 3, 7, 8); it never proves a number IS a square.

questions.stem: Without long multiplication, find 41² using the pattern (40 + 1)².
How many natural numbers lie between 24² and 25²?
questions.answer: 2 × 24 = 48 numbers (between n² and (n+1)² there are 2n numbers).
questions.markingKey: 2 × 24 = 48 numbers (between n² and (n+1)² there are 2n numbers).

questions.stem: Find the smallest number by which 392 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square, and find the square root of the result.
In the prime-factorisation method, what must be true of the exponent of every prime for the number to be a perfect square?
questions.answer: Every exponent must be even (the primes pair up).
questions.markingKey: Every exponent must be even (the primes pair up).

questions.stem: Explain in one line why √(a × b) = √a × √b makes √3600 easy.
A student writes √(16 + 9) = √16 + √9 = 7. Show the error with a check.
questions.answer: √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5, not 7. Square roots do not distribute over addition.
questions.markingKey: √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5, not 7. Square roots do not distribute over addition.

questions.stem: Find √1764 by prime factorisation.
Estimate √56 to one decimal place without a calculator.
A square garden has area 6.25 m². A path 0.5 m wide is built all around it. Find the outer side length of the path.
Find the least number that must be subtracted from 2000 to make it a perfect square, and give the square root of the result.
1225 chairs are arranged with rows = columns. 24 more chairs arrive. Can all chairs still form a square arrangement? If not, what is the least number of extra chairs needed?
Which of these is a perfect cube: 100, 125, 150, 200?
In one line: why can a perfect cube end in any digit 0–9, while a square cannot?
questions.answer: The cubes of 0–9 end in 0,1,8,7,4,5,6,3,2,9 — every digit appears, whereas squares end only in 0,1,4,5,6,9.
questions.markingKey: The cubes of 0–9 end in 0,1,8,7,4,5,6,3,2,9 — every digit appears, whereas squares end only in 0,1,4,5,6,9.

questions.stem: Explain why doubling the side of a cube makes its volume 8 times, not 2 times.
questions.answer: (2s)³ = 8s³: each of the three dimensions doubles, so the volume multiplies by 2 × 2 × 2.
questions.markingKey: (2s)³ = 8s³: each of the three dimensions doubles, so the volume multiplies by 2 × 2 × 2.

questions.stem: Find ∛3375 by prime factorisation.
Find the smallest number by which 243 must be divided to get a perfect cube.
Cuboids of size 5 cm × 2 cm × 5 cm are stacked to make a solid cube. How many cuboids are needed and what is the side of the cube?
questions.answer: Volume 50 = 2 × 5². To make every prime's exponent a multiple of 3 we need 2² × 5 = 20 cuboids; volume 1000 cm³, side 10 cm.
questions.markingKey: Volume 50 = 2 × 5². To make every prime's exponent a multiple of 3 we need 2² × 5 = 20 cuboids; volume 1000 cm³, side 10 cm.

questions.stem: For a natural number m > 1, (2m, m² − 1, m² + 1) is a Pythagorean triplet. Which member is always the largest?
Explain in one line why (3, 4, 5) and (6, 8, 10) are both triplets.
questions.answer: (6, 8, 10) is (3, 4, 5) scaled by 2; 36 + 64 = 100 still holds because every term gets multiplied by 4.
questions.markingKey: (6, 8, 10) is (3, 4, 5) scaled by 2; 36 + 64 = 100 still holds because every term gets multiplied by 4.

questions.stem: Is (5, 12, 13) produced by the formula (2m, m² − 1, m² + 1) for some natural number m? What does this tell you about the formula?
questions.answer: No: the even member 12 would give 2m = 12, m = 6, but then m² − 1 = 35 ≠ 5. The formula gives many triplets but not all of them.
questions.markingKey: No: the even member 12 would give 2m = 12, m = 6, but then m² − 1 = 35 ≠ 5. The formula gives many triplets but not all of them.

questions.stem: Use the formula to find a triplet whose smallest member is 8.
Find a Pythagorean triplet in which 17 is a member.
The sum of a natural number and its square is 132. Find the number using the table of squares (no formulas).
Simplify 2⁵ ÷ 2². (a) 2³ (b) 2⁷ (c) 1³ (d) 2^(5/2)
Explain in one line why (2³)² is not equal to 2^(3+2).
questions.answer: A power of a power multiplies exponents: (2³)² = 2⁶ = 64, whereas 2⁵ = 32.
questions.markingKey: A power of a power multiplies exponents: (2³)² = 2⁶ = 64, whereas 2⁵ = 32.

questions.stem: A student writes 2³ × 3² = 6⁵. Show why this is wrong.
questions.answer: 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72, but 6⁵ = 7776. The product law aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ needs the SAME base.
questions.markingKey: 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72, but 6⁵ = 7776. The product law aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ needs the SAME base.

questions.stem: Simplify (5⁴ × 5³) ÷ 5⁵.
Simplify (2³ × 3⁴ × 4) ÷ (3² × 32).
If 3ˣ × 3⁴ = 3¹⁰ ÷ 3², find x, and then find the value of 3ˣ ÷ 9.
Simplify [(a³b²)² × a⁴] ÷ (a⁵b³).
A bacteria colony doubles every hour. It starts with 2³ bacteria. (i) After 5 hours the count is 2ⁿ; find n. (ii) After how many hours (whole) does the count first EXCEED 2¹⁵?
questions.answer: (i) 2³ × 2⁵ = 2⁸, n = 8 (do not add 5 to the base). (ii) 2^(3+t) > 2¹⁵ → t > 12 → after 13 hours (at 12 h it equals 2¹⁵, not exceeds).
questions.markingKey: (i) 2³ × 2⁵ = 2⁸, n = 8 (do not add 5 to the base). (ii) 2^(3+t) > 2¹⁵ → t > 12 → after 13 hours (at 12 h it equals 2¹⁵, not exceeds).

questions.stem: Write the values of 7⁰ and 2⁻³.
Using a³ ÷ a³, explain in one line why a⁰ = 1.
questions.answer: a³ ÷ a³ = a³⁻³ = a⁰, and any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
questions.markingKey: a³ ÷ a³ = a³⁻³ = a⁰, and any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

questions.stem: Why is (−2)⁻² positive but (−2)⁻³ negative?
Evaluate (2/3)⁻².
Simplify 5⁻³ × 5⁵ ÷ 5⁻¹.
Find x if (1/2)ˣ = 16.
Write 3.2 × 10⁵ in usual form.
Why is 32 × 10⁴ not in standard form? Write it correctly.
questions.answer: The coefficient must satisfy 1 ≤ a < 10. Correct form: 3.2 × 10⁵.
questions.markingKey: The coefficient must satisfy 1 ≤ a < 10. Correct form: 3.2 × 10⁵.

questions.stem: Which is larger, 4.5 × 10⁻³ or 9 × 10⁻⁴, and by what factor?
Write 0.000067 in standard form.
Earth–Sun distance ≈ 1.5 × 10⁸ km; speed of light = 3 × 10⁵ km/s. How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
One hydrogen atom has mass 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. About how many atoms are in 1 g of hydrogen? Answer in standard form.
What is the value of the Roman numeral XIV?
Which Indian mathematician first wrote down rules for calculating with zero?
In one line: why did the place-value system make calculation easier than Roman numerals?
questions.answer: The value of a digit depends on its position, so only ten symbols are needed and numbers can be added or multiplied column by column.
questions.markingKey: The value of a digit depends on its position, so only ten symbols are needed and numbers can be added or multiplied column by column.

questions.stem: Write 2035 in Roman numerals.
Convert MCMXLVII to Hindu-Arabic numerals, add 53, and write the answer back in Roman numerals.
Define a rational number. Is 0 a rational number?
questions.answer: A number that can be written as p/q with p, q integers and q ≠ 0. Yes, 0 = 0/1.
questions.markingKey: A number that can be written as p/q with p, q integers and q ≠ 0. Yes, 0 = 0/1.

questions.stem: Explain in one line why rational numbers are closed under subtraction but natural numbers are not.
questions.answer: 2 − 5 = −3 is not a natural number, but the difference of two rationals is always a rational.
questions.markingKey: 2 − 5 = −3 is not a natural number, but the difference of two rationals is always a rational.

questions.stem: Give an example showing that division of rational numbers is not associative.
Find the additive inverse and the multiplicative inverse of −7/9, then multiply the two inverses.
Use the distributive property to evaluate 7/5 × (−3/12) + 7/5 × 5/12.
A tank was 3/5 full. 1/4 of the tank's capacity was used, then 2/15 of the capacity was added. What fraction is now full? If the tank holds 600 L, how many litres are in it?
How many rational numbers lie between 1/3 and 1/2?
Explain in one line how the mean helps find a rational number between 1/3 and 1/2.
questions.answer: The mean (1/3 + 1/2)/2 = 5/12 always lies between the two numbers.
questions.markingKey: The mean (1/3 + 1/2)/2 = 5/12 always lies between the two numbers.

questions.stem: A student says −3/4 lies to the right of −1/2 because 3 > 1. Correct the student using the number line.
questions.answer: −3/4 = −0.75 is further LEFT of 0 than −0.5, so −3/4 < −1/2.
questions.markingKey: −3/4 = −0.75 is further LEFT of 0 than −0.5, so −3/4 < −1/2.

questions.stem: Between which two integers does 7/4 lie, and where exactly is it on a number line divided into quarters?
questions.answer: Between 1 and 2, at 1¾ (the third mark after 1).
questions.markingKey: Between 1 and 2, at 1¾ (the third mark after 1).

questions.stem: Write three rational numbers between −2/5 and 1/5.
Write five rational numbers between 3/5 and 4/5 in increasing order.
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is called a ______.
In one line: why is every square a rhombus, but not every rhombus a square?
questions.answer: Both have four equal sides; a square additionally needs four right angles.
questions.markingKey: Both have four equal sides; a square additionally needs four right angles.

questions.stem: A kite has two pairs of equal ADJACENT sides. Explain why a rhombus is a special kind of kite.
questions.answer: In a rhombus all four sides are equal, so both pairs of adjacent sides are equal — it satisfies the kite condition.
questions.markingKey: In a rhombus all four sides are equal, so both pairs of adjacent sides are equal — it satisfies the kite condition.

questions.stem: Name the quadrilateral whose diagonals are equal and bisect each other at right angles.
A quadrilateral has sides 5, 5, 8, 8 cm with the equal sides adjacent; its diagonals are unequal and one bisects the other at 90°. Name it.
Describe a quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other but are neither equal nor perpendicular. Name it and justify.
questions.answer: A parallelogram (non-rectangle, non-rhombus): bisecting diagonals ⇒ parallelogram; not equal ⇒ not a rectangle; not perpendicular ⇒ not a rhombus.
questions.markingKey: A parallelogram (non-rectangle, non-rhombus): bisecting diagonals ⇒ parallelogram; not equal ⇒ not a rectangle; not perpendicular ⇒ not a rhombus.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of (i) a quadrilateral, (ii) a hexagon?
Using one diagonal, explain in one line why the angle sum of a quadrilateral is 360°.
questions.answer: A diagonal splits it into two triangles, each with angle sum 180°.
questions.markingKey: A diagonal splits it into two triangles, each with angle sum 180°.

questions.stem: Why is the sum of the exterior angles of ANY polygon 360°, regardless of the number of sides?
questions.answer: Walking around the polygon you turn through each exterior angle and end up facing the same way, i.e. one full turn = 360°.
questions.markingKey: Walking around the polygon you turn through each exterior angle and end up facing the same way, i.e. one full turn = 360°.

questions.stem: The angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95°, 100° and x. Find x.
Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. How many sides does it have?
The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 6. Find them. Can this quadrilateral be a trapezium (a pair of co-interior angles adding to 180°)?
questions.answer: Angles 48°, 72°, 96°, 144°. No two of them add to 180°, so it cannot be a trapezium in any arrangement.
questions.markingKey: Angles 48°, 72°, 96°, 144°. No two of them add to 180°, so it cannot be a trapezium in any arrangement.

questions.stem: State one diagonal property that a rectangle has but a general parallelogram does not.
questions.answer: Its diagonals are equal in length.
questions.markingKey: Its diagonals are equal in length.

questions.stem: In one line: why are opposite angles of a parallelogram equal?
questions.answer: Each pair of adjacent angles adds to 180° (co-interior angles), so angles opposite each other are both supplements of the same angle.
questions.markingKey: Each pair of adjacent angles adds to 180° (co-interior angles), so angles opposite each other are both supplements of the same angle.

questions.stem: A student says 'a quadrilateral with equal diagonals must be a rectangle.' Give a counter-example.
questions.answer: An isosceles trapezium has equal diagonals but is not a rectangle.
questions.markingKey: An isosceles trapezium has equal diagonals but is not a rectangle.

questions.stem: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B, ∠C and ∠D.
The diagonals of a rhombus are 12 cm and 16 cm. Find its side.
Two adjacent angles of a parallelogram are (3x + 10)° and (2x + 20)°. Find all four angles.
Diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at O. PO = 3y − 1 and OR = y + 5. Find y and the length PR.
questions.answer: Diagonals bisect: 3y − 1 = y + 5 → y = 3; PO = 8, PR = 16.
questions.markingKey: Diagonals bisect: 3y − 1 = y + 5 → y = 3; PO = 8, PR = 16.

questions.stem: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and ∠AOB = 60°. Show that triangle AOB is equilateral and find ∠OAD.
questions.answer: OA = OB (halves of equal diagonals) and the vertex angle is 60°, so the base angles are 60° each → equilateral. ∠OAB = 60°, so ∠OAD = 90° − 60° = 30°.
questions.markingKey: OA = OB (halves of equal diagonals) and the vertex angle is 60°, so the base angles are 60° each → equilateral. ∠OAB = 60°, so ∠OAD = 90° − 60° = 30°.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of independent measurements needed to construct a unique quadrilateral?
In one line: why can't a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely from its four sides alone?
questions.answer: Four hinged sides can flex into many shapes; a diagonal or an angle is needed to fix it.
questions.markingKey: Four hinged sides can flex into many shapes; a diagonal or an angle is needed to fix it.

questions.stem: Can you construct quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm and diagonal AC = 10 cm? Explain.
questions.answer: No: in triangle ABC, 3 + 4 < 10 violates the triangle inequality.
questions.markingKey: No: in triangle ABC, 3 + 4 < 10 violates the triangle inequality.

questions.stem: Outline the steps to construct ABCD with AB = 4 cm, BC = 5 cm, CD = 6 cm, DA = 4.5 cm, AC = 7 cm.
questions.answer: Draw triangle ABC (AB = 4, BC = 5, AC = 7); from A cut an arc of 4.5 cm and from C an arc of 6 cm; their intersection is D; join AD, CD.
questions.markingKey: Draw triangle ABC (AB = 4, BC = 5, AC = 7); from A cut an arc of 4.5 cm and from C an arc of 6 cm; their intersection is D; join AD, CD.

questions.stem: Describe how to construct a rhombus with diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm.
questions.answer: Draw AC = 8 cm, construct its perpendicular bisector, mark B and D 3 cm on either side of the midpoint, join. (Side comes out as 5 cm.)
questions.markingKey: Draw AC = 8 cm, construct its perpendicular bisector, mark B and D 3 cm on either side of the midpoint, join. (Side comes out as 5 cm.)

questions.stem: Which data sets give a UNIQUE quadrilateral? (i) 4 sides + 1 angle (ii) 3 sides + 2 included angles (iii) 2 adjacent sides + 3 angles (iv) 4 angles + 1 side.
questions.answer: (i), (ii) and (iii) yes. (iv) no — the same angles with one side fixed still allow different shapes (only one side is fixed, the others can vary).
questions.markingKey: (i), (ii) and (iii) yes. (iv) no — the same angles with one side fixed still allow different shapes (only one side is fixed, the others can vary).

questions.stem: State the divisibility rules for 3 and for 9.
questions.answer: Divisible by 3 if the digit sum is divisible by 3; by 9 if the digit sum is divisible by 9.
questions.markingKey: Divisible by 3 if the digit sum is divisible by 3; by 9 if the digit sum is divisible by 9.

questions.stem: In one line: why does the rule for 4 look only at the last two digits?
questions.answer: Every hundred is divisible by 4, so only the part below 100 (the last two digits) matters.
questions.markingKey: Every hundred is divisible by 4, so only the part below 100 (the last two digits) matters.

questions.stem: A number is divisible by 4 and by 6. A student concludes it is divisible by 24. Give a counter-example.
questions.answer: 12 is divisible by 4 and 6 but not by 24 (LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, not 24).
questions.markingKey: 12 is divisible by 4 and 6 but not by 24 (LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, not 24).

questions.stem: Is 5832 divisible by 9? By 6?
questions.answer: Digit sum 18 → divisible by 9. It is even and divisible by 3 → divisible by 6. Yes to both.
questions.markingKey: Digit sum 18 → divisible by 9. It is even and divisible by 3 → divisible by 6. Yes to both.

questions.stem: Find all digits x for which 31x5 is divisible by 3.
questions.answer: 9 + x must be a multiple of 3 → x = 0, 3, 6 or 9.
questions.markingKey: 9 + x must be a multiple of 3 → x = 0, 3, 6 or 9.

questions.stem: Find the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 11.
In a 3 × 3 magic square using 1 to 9, what is the magic sum?
In one line: why must the magic sum be 15?
questions.answer: 1 + 2 + … + 9 = 45 is shared equally by three rows: 45 ÷ 3 = 15.
questions.markingKey: 1 + 2 + … + 9 = 45 is shared equally by three rows: 45 ÷ 3 = 15.

questions.stem: Explain why 5 must be in the centre of a 1–9 magic square.
questions.answer: The centre lies on 4 lines (row, column, 2 diagonals); only 5 can pair with the remaining numbers in four different ways to make 15.
questions.markingKey: The centre lies on 4 lines (row, column, 2 diagonals); only 5 can pair with the remaining numbers in four different ways to make 15.

questions.stem: Complete the magic square: row 1: 8, _, 6; row 2: _, 5, _; row 3: 4, _, 2.
Using 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2, find the sum 1 + 2 + … + 40.
Triangular numbers are 1, 3, 6, 10, … Which triangular number is 210 (i.e. find n)?
State two basic rules of letters-for-digits puzzles.
questions.answer: Each letter stands for exactly one digit (and each digit for one letter); the first digit of a number cannot be 0.
questions.markingKey: Each letter stands for exactly one digit (and each digit for one letter); the first digit of a number cannot be 0.

questions.stem: In A + A = 1B, explain in one line why A must be at least 5.
questions.answer: A + A ≥ 10 for the sum to have two digits, so A ≥ 5.
questions.markingKey: A + A ≥ 10 for the sum to have two digits, so A ≥ 5.

questions.stem: If A × A ends in the digit A, what can A be? Explain.
Solve: 3A + 25 = B2 (two-digit numbers).
questions.answer: Units: A + 5 ends in 2 → A = 7; 37 + 25 = 62 → B = 6.
questions.markingKey: Units: A + 5 ends in 2 → A = 7; 37 + 25 = 62 → B = 6.

questions.stem: Solve AB + BA = 121. What can you say about A and B?
Solve AB × 6 = BBB.
questions.answer: BBB = 111 × B, so AB = 18.5 × B → B must be even. B = 2 gives 37 (37 × 6 = 222); B = 4 gives 74 (74 × 6 = 444). Two solutions.
questions.markingKey: BBB = 111 × B, so AB = 18.5 × B → B must be even. B = 2 gives 37 (37 × 6 = 222); B = 4 gives 74 (74 × 6 = 444). Two solutions.

questions.stem: Write 7 × (20 + 3) using the distributive property and evaluate.
In one line: why is 15 × 98 = 15 × 100 − 15 × 2 quicker?
questions.answer: 98 = 100 − 2, so it becomes 1500 − 30 = 1470 with no carrying.
questions.markingKey: 98 = 100 − 2, so it becomes 1500 − 30 = 1470 with no carrying.

questions.stem: Why is 12 × (5 × 4) NOT equal to (12 × 5) × (12 × 4)?
questions.answer: Multiplication distributes over addition, not over multiplication: 12 × 20 = 240 but 60 × 48 = 2880.
questions.markingKey: Multiplication distributes over addition, not over multiplication: 12 × 20 = 240 but 60 × 48 = 2880.

questions.stem: Evaluate 25 × 104 mentally.
Evaluate 37 × 46 + 37 × 54.
In 4x²y − 3xy + 7, what is the coefficient of xy and what is the constant term?
In one line: why can 3x² and 5x not be combined into one term?
questions.answer: They have different powers of x, so they are unlike terms.
questions.markingKey: They have different powers of x, so they are unlike terms.

questions.stem: Which of these are like terms: 2ab, −3ba, 4a²b, ab²?
Add 3x + 5y − 2 and 4x − 7y + 6.
Subtract 5a² − 3a + 4 from 7a² + 2a − 1.
A triangle has sides 2x + 3, 3x − 1 and x + 7. Its perimeter is 33. Find x and the three sides. What kind of triangle is it?
In one line: why does (x + 2)(x + 3) end with three terms although four products are formed?
questions.answer: The two middle products 3x and 2x are like terms and combine.
questions.markingKey: The two middle products 3x and 2x are like terms and combine.

questions.stem: A student writes (a + b)(a + b) = a² + b². Show the error with a = 1, b = 1.
questions.answer: (1 + 1)² = 4 but 1² + 1² = 2; the cross term 2ab is missing.
questions.markingKey: (1 + 1)² = 4 but 1² + 1² = 2; the cross term 2ab is missing.

questions.stem: Expand 5x(2x − 3y).
Expand (2x + 5)(x − 4).
A rectangle has length (3a + 2) m and breadth (a − 1) m. Write an expression for its area and find the area when a = 4.
Simplify (x + 3)(x + 5) − (x − 2)(x + 2).
A cuboid has edges (x + 1), (x − 1) and 2x. Find its volume as an expression, then verify for x = 3 by direct multiplication.
Simplify the ratio 45 : 60.
In one line: why are 2 : 3 and 3 : 2 different?
questions.answer: Order matters — the first number compares to the second; 2 : 3 = 0.67 while 3 : 2 = 1.5.
questions.markingKey: Order matters — the first number compares to the second; 2 : 3 = 0.67 while 3 : 2 = 1.5.

questions.stem: Which ratio is larger, 3 : 4 or 5 : 7? Show how you decided.
6 pens cost ₹84. Find the cost of 10 pens.
Divide ₹1200 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5.
Boys : girls in a class of 45 is 5 : 4. Five more girls join. Find the new ratio.
If x and y are in direct proportion, which quantity stays constant?
Is a person's age and height in direct proportion? Explain in one line.
questions.answer: No — the ratio height/age is not constant (a 40-year-old is not twice as tall as a 20-year-old).
questions.markingKey: No — the ratio height/age is not constant (a 40-year-old is not twice as tall as a 20-year-old).

questions.stem: x: 2, 4, 6 and y: 5, 10, 15.5. Are x and y in direct proportion?
A cyclist covers 12 km in 1.5 h. At the same speed, how far in 4 h?
A map scale is 1 cm : 20 km. Two cities are 6.5 cm apart on the map. Actual distance?
A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g flour and 2 eggs. Scale it for 10 people. Is the egg answer sensible?
questions.answer: 750 g flour and 5 eggs — sensible (whole number; if it came out fractional you would round up).
questions.markingKey: 750 g flour and 5 eggs — sensible (whole number; if it came out fractional you would round up).

questions.stem: If x and y are in inverse proportion, which quantity is constant?
In one line: why are speed and time (for a fixed distance) in inverse proportion?
questions.answer: Speed × time = distance, which is constant.
questions.markingKey: Speed × time = distance, which is constant.

questions.stem: A student says 'more workers means more days to finish.' Correct the statement.
questions.answer: More workers, FEWER days: workers × days is constant (inverse proportion).
questions.markingKey: More workers, FEWER days: workers × days is constant (inverse proportion).

questions.stem: 8 workers finish a job in 12 days. How many days for 6 workers?
A car at 60 km/h takes 5 h. Time at 75 km/h?
A shelf holds 20 boxes of 12 kg each at its weight limit. How many 15 kg boxes can it hold?
Food lasts 40 students for 30 days. After 10 days, 10 more students join. How many more days will the food last?
Tap A fills a tank in 6 h and tap B in 3 h. How long do both together take? (Decide first whether this is an inverse-proportion problem.)
questions.answer: It is a rates problem, not simple inverse proportion: in 1 h they fill 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the tank → 2 h.
questions.markingKey: It is a rates problem, not simple inverse proportion: in 1 h they fill 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the tank → 2 h.

questions.stem: Write 3/8 as a decimal.
In one line: why are 0.5, 5/10 and 1/2 the same number?
questions.answer: They are equivalent forms: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, and 1/2 = 0.5.
questions.markingKey: They are equivalent forms: 5/10 simplifies to 1/2, and 1/2 = 0.5.

questions.stem: A student writes 0.25 = 1/25. Correct it.
Write 0.64 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Which is larger, 7/12 or 0.58?
Find the fraction equivalent to 5/8 whose numerator and denominator add to 65.
Write 1/3 as a decimal. Is it terminating or recurring?
In one line: how can you tell from the denominator (lowest terms) whether a fraction terminates?
questions.answer: It terminates only if the denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.
questions.markingKey: It terminates only if the denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.

questions.stem: Does 7/12 have a terminating decimal? Explain.
Write 5/6 as a recurring decimal.
Write 0.4444… as a fraction.
Write 0.2727… as a fraction in lowest terms and check by division.
Which is larger, 2/5 or 3/5?
Arrange 0.7, 0.65, 0.703 in increasing order.
In one line: why is 3/7 smaller than 3/5?
questions.answer: Same number of pieces, but sevenths are smaller pieces than fifths.
questions.markingKey: Same number of pieces, but sevenths are smaller pieces than fifths.

questions.stem: Arrange 2/3, 5/8, 0.6, 7/10 in ascending order.
Ria read 3/8 of a book, Sam read 0.4 of it and Tia read 2/5. Who read the most? Did any two read the same amount?
questions.answer: Sam and Tia both read 0.4 (= 2/5), which is more than 3/8 = 0.375.
questions.markingKey: Sam and Tia both read 0.4 (= 2/5), which is more than 3/8 = 0.375.

questions.stem: State the Baudhayana–Pythagoras theorem.
questions.answer: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
questions.markingKey: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

questions.stem: In one line: why is the theorem named after Baudhayana as well as Pythagoras?
questions.answer: Baudhayana stated it in the Sulbasutras (c. 800 BCE), centuries before Pythagoras.
questions.markingKey: Baudhayana stated it in the Sulbasutras (c. 800 BCE), centuries before Pythagoras.

questions.stem: Four identical right triangles (legs a, b, hypotenuse c) are placed inside a square of side (a + b), leaving a tilted square of side c. In one line, explain how this proves c² = a² + b².
questions.answer: (a + b)² = 4 × (½ab) + c² → a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c² → c² = a² + b².
questions.markingKey: (a + b)² = 4 × (½ab) + c² → a² + 2ab + b² = 2ab + c² → c² = a² + b².

questions.stem: Verify the theorem for the triangle with sides 6, 8, 10.
Does 7, 24, 25 satisfy the theorem?
Which of these CANNOT be the sides of a right triangle: (9, 12, 15), (5, 6, 8), (8, 15, 17)?
questions.answer: (5, 6, 8): 25 + 36 = 61 ≠ 64. The other two satisfy the theorem.
questions.markingKey: (5, 6, 8): 25 + 36 = 61 ≠ 64. The other two satisfy the theorem.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 5 cm and 12 cm. Find the hypotenuse.
In one line: why can the hypotenuse never be shorter than a leg?
questions.answer: c² = a² + b² > a², so c > a (and similarly c > b).
questions.markingKey: c² = a² + b² > a², so c > a (and similarly c > b).

questions.stem: Hypotenuse 10, one leg 6. A student writes 'other leg = √(100 + 36)'. Fix it.
A 13 m ladder has its foot 5 m from a wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
Find the diagonal of a rectangle 24 cm by 7 cm.
A pole broke and its top touched the ground 12 m from its base; the broken part is 13 m long. What was the original height?
questions.answer: Standing part = √(169 − 144) = 5 m; original height = 5 + 13 = 18 m.
questions.markingKey: Standing part = √(169 − 144) = 5 m; original height = 5 + 13 = 18 m.

questions.stem: Find the diagonal of a square of side 10 cm, first in surd form, then to 1 decimal place.
A person walks 5 km north, then 4 km east, then 7 km north. How far (straight line) is she from the start, to 1 decimal place?
questions.answer: Net 12 km north and 4 km east → √(144 + 16) = √160 ≈ 12.6 km.
questions.markingKey: Net 12 km north and 4 km east → √(144 + 16) = √160 ≈ 12.6 km.

questions.stem: State the converse of the theorem.
questions.answer: If a² + b² = c² for the sides of a triangle, then the angle opposite side c is a right angle.
questions.markingKey: If a² + b² = c² for the sides of a triangle, then the angle opposite side c is a right angle.

questions.stem: In one line: why do builders stretch a rope knotted at 3, 4 and 5 units?
questions.answer: 3² + 4² = 5², so the corner formed is exactly a right angle.
questions.markingKey: 3² + 4² = 5², so the corner formed is exactly a right angle.

questions.stem: Is a triangle with sides 5, 5, 5 right-angled? Explain.
Is the triangle with sides 20, 21, 29 right-angled?
On a square grid, find the distance between (0, 0) and (6, 8).
A TV screen has a 40-inch diagonal and is 32 inches wide. Find its height. Is the width : height ratio 4 : 3?
Write 3/8 as a percentage.
In one line: why does a 50% increase followed by a 50% decrease NOT return to the start?
questions.answer: The decrease is taken on the larger amount: 100 → 150 → 75.
questions.markingKey: The decrease is taken on the larger amount: 100 → 150 → 75.

questions.stem: Is 20% of 50 equal to 50% of 20? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes, both are 10: a% of b = b% of a because a × b/100 = b × a/100.
questions.markingKey: Yes, both are 10: a% of b = b% of a because a × b/100 = b × a/100.

questions.stem: Find 15% of 240.
A price rises from ₹1200 to ₹1380. Find the percentage increase.
A town's population of 25 000 increased by 8% and then decreased by 5%. Find the final population.
Write the formula for profit percentage.
In one line: why is discount calculated on the marked price but profit on the cost price?
questions.answer: Discount is a reduction offered from the price displayed (MP); profit is the gain compared with what the seller paid (CP).
questions.markingKey: Discount is a reduction offered from the price displayed (MP); profit is the gain compared with what the seller paid (CP).

questions.stem: A student says: 'Sold for ₹100 at 20% profit, so the cost price was ₹80.' Is this right?
questions.answer: No: CP = 100 ÷ 1.20 = ₹83.33. Twenty percent of CP, not of SP, is the profit.
questions.markingKey: No: CP = 100 ÷ 1.20 = ₹83.33. Twenty percent of CP, not of SP, is the profit.

questions.stem: CP = ₹450, SP = ₹540. Find the profit percentage.
Marked price ₹2000, discount 15%. Find the selling price, then the amount payable after 5% GST on the selling price.
An article was sold for ₹1150 at a loss of 8%. Find the cost price.
Two chairs were bought for ₹800 each. One was sold at 10% profit and the other at 10% loss. Find the overall gain or loss.
questions.answer: ₹880 + ₹720 = ₹1600 = total CP → no gain, no loss.
questions.markingKey: ₹880 + ₹720 = ₹1600 = total CP → no gain, no loss.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks goods 40% above cost and gives 20% discount. (i) Find the profit %. (ii) What discount on the same marked price would give exactly 5% profit?
questions.answer: (i) 1.40 × 0.80 = 1.12 → 12% profit. (ii) SP must be 1.05 CP = 0.75 MP → 25% discount.
questions.markingKey: (i) 1.40 × 0.80 = 1.12 → 12% profit. (ii) SP must be 1.05 CP = 0.75 MP → 25% discount.

questions.stem: Write the formula for simple interest.
In one line: why is compound interest more than simple interest after the first year?
questions.answer: From year 2 onward, interest is also earned on the previously added interest.
questions.markingKey: From year 2 onward, interest is also earned on the previously added interest.

questions.stem: A student says CI on ₹1000 for 2 years at 10% is ₹200. Correct it.
Find the SI on ₹5000 at 6% p.a. for 3 years.
Find the CI on ₹8000 at 5% p.a. for 2 years.
₹10 000 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year. Find the interest.
In how many years will ₹8000 earn ₹2400 simple interest at 5% p.a.?
At what rate of compound interest (annual) will ₹6250 grow to ₹7290 in 2 years?
How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
What is the order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle?
In one line: why does a parallelogram have rotational symmetry of order 2 but no line of symmetry?
questions.answer: Turning it 180° about the centre maps it onto itself, but no fold makes the two halves coincide because its angles are not right angles.
questions.markingKey: Turning it 180° about the centre maps it onto itself, but no fold makes the two halves coincide because its angles are not right angles.

questions.stem: For the letter H, state the number of lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry.
Give two shapes with rotational symmetry of order 4 AND 4 lines of symmetry, and one shape with order 4 but NO line of symmetry.
questions.answer: Square, plus sign (+); a pinwheel with four identical curved blades has order 4 but no line symmetry.
questions.markingKey: Square, plus sign (+); a pinwheel with four identical curved blades has order 4 but no line symmetry.

questions.stem: Which two instruments are used in a classical geometric construction?
In one line: why is every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB equidistant from A and B?
questions.answer: The bisector is the set of points where the two arcs of equal radius from A and B meet, so distances to A and B are equal by construction.
questions.markingKey: The bisector is the set of points where the two arcs of equal radius from A and B meet, so distances to A and B are equal by construction.

questions.stem: Can a 45° angle be constructed without a protractor? Explain.
Describe how to construct a 60° angle and then a 30° angle.
questions.answer: With centre at the vertex draw an arc; with the same radius from where it cuts the arm cut the arc again; join to get 60°. Bisect this angle for 30°.
questions.markingKey: With centre at the vertex draw an arc; with the same radius from where it cuts the arm cut the arc again; join to get 60°. Bisect this angle for 30°.

questions.stem: Describe how to construct a triangle with sides 4, 5, 6 cm and locate the point equidistant from all three vertices.
questions.answer: Draw 6 cm base; arcs of 4 cm and 5 cm from the ends meet at the third vertex. Draw perpendicular bisectors of two sides; their intersection (circumcentre) is equidistant from the vertices.
questions.markingKey: Draw 6 cm base; arcs of 4 cm and 5 cm from the ends meet at the third vertex. Draw perpendicular bisectors of two sides; their intersection (circumcentre) is equidistant from the vertices.

questions.stem: Construct a regular hexagon inside a circle of radius 3 cm. Explain why stepping the radius around the circle works.
questions.answer: Mark 6 arcs of radius 3 cm around the circle and join. It works because the centre and two adjacent vertices form an equilateral triangle (central angle 60°), so each side equals the radius.
questions.markingKey: Mark 6 arcs of radius 3 cm around the circle and join. It works because the centre and two adjacent vertices form an equilateral triangle (central angle 60°), so each side equals the radius.

questions.stem: What is a tessellation?
questions.answer: A covering of the plane with shapes leaving no gaps and no overlaps.
questions.markingKey: A covering of the plane with shapes leaving no gaps and no overlaps.

questions.stem: Which regular polygons tessellate on their own?
In one line: why can't regular pentagons tessellate?
questions.answer: Each angle is 108°, which does not divide 360°.
questions.markingKey: Each angle is 108°, which does not divide 360°.

questions.stem: How many regular hexagons meet at each vertex of a hexagonal tiling?
A tiling uses squares and regular octagons around each vertex. Check that it works using angles.
questions.answer: 90° + 135° + 135° = 360° ✓ (one square and two octagons at each vertex).
questions.markingKey: 90° + 135° + 135° = 360° ✓ (one square and two octagons at each vertex).

questions.stem: Write the coordinates of the origin. Which axis is horizontal?
In one line: why is (3, 5) a different point from (5, 3)?
questions.answer: The first number is always the x-distance and the second the y-distance, so swapping them moves the point.
questions.markingKey: The first number is always the x-distance and the second the y-distance, so swapping them moves the point.

questions.stem: Which coordinate is zero for every point on the y-axis? Where exactly is (0, −4)?
questions.answer: x = 0; (0, −4) is on the y-axis, 4 units below the origin.
questions.markingKey: x = 0; (0, −4) is on the y-axis, 4 units below the origin.

questions.stem: A(2, 3) and B(6, 3) are plotted. Find the length AB.
Three vertices of a rectangle are (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4). Find the fourth.
A triangle has vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (0, 8). Find its perimeter.
On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal segment mean?
questions.answer: The object is at rest (distance not changing).
questions.markingKey: The object is at rest (distance not changing).

questions.stem: In one line: why is a line graph better than a bar graph for temperature over a day?
questions.answer: Temperature changes continuously, and a line lets you read values between the measured times.
questions.markingKey: Temperature changes continuously, and a line lets you read values between the measured times.

questions.stem: Two objects' distance–time lines start together; one is steeper. What does the steeper line show?
questions.answer: Higher speed (more distance per unit time).
questions.markingKey: Higher speed (more distance per unit time).

questions.stem: A graph shows 0 km at 0 h and 60 km at 2 h along a straight line. Find the speed.
Temperatures: 6 am 18°C, 9 am 24°C, 12 pm 30°C, 3 pm 28°C. Plot a line graph and estimate the temperature at 10:30 am.
A cyclist's graph shows 40 km covered in 3.5 h including a 0.5 h stop. Find the average speed for the whole trip and the average speed while moving.
For y = 2x, find y when x = 5.
In one line: why does the graph of cost = 5 × (weight in kg) pass through the origin?
Why does the graph of y = 2x + 3 NOT pass through the origin?
questions.answer: There is a fixed part 3: when x = 0, y = 3.
questions.markingKey: There is a fixed part 3: when x = 0, y = 3.

questions.stem: x: 0, 1, 2, 3 and y: 3, 5, 7, 9. Write the rule connecting y and x.
A taxi charges ₹50 fixed plus ₹12 per km. Write the rule, sketch the graph, and find the fare for 8 km.
Plan A costs ₹100 + ₹5 per unit; Plan B costs ₹8 per unit. Draw both lines. At how many units do they cost the same, and which is cheaper for 40 units?
questions.answer: 100 + 5u = 8u → u = 33⅓; for 40 units A = ₹300, B = ₹320 → A is cheaper.
questions.markingKey: 100 + 5u = 8u → u = 33⅓; for 40 units A = ₹300, B = ₹320 → A is cheaper.

questions.stem: Complete: (a − b)² = ______.
In one line: using the area model, why does (a + b)² contain the term 2ab?
questions.answer: A square of side (a + b) splits into an a × a square, a b × b square and TWO a × b rectangles.
questions.markingKey: A square of side (a + b) splits into an a × a square, a b × b square and TWO a × b rectangles.

questions.stem: A student writes (a + b)² = a² + b². Test with a = 3, b = 4.
questions.answer: (3 + 4)² = 49 but 9 + 16 = 25; the missing 2ab = 24 makes the difference.
questions.markingKey: (3 + 4)² = 49 but 9 + 16 = 25; the missing 2ab = 24 makes the difference.

questions.stem: Expand (3x + 2)².
Evaluate 103² using an identity.
Evaluate 9.8 × 10.2 using an identity.
If x + 1/x = 5, find x² + 1/x².
Simplify (2a + 3b)² − (2a − 3b)², then evaluate for a = 2.5, b = 1/3.
What is the highest common factor of 12x² and 18x?
In one line: how is factorising related to expanding?
questions.answer: Factorising is expanding in reverse — writing an expression as a product of its factors.
questions.markingKey: Factorising is expanding in reverse — writing an expression as a product of its factors.

questions.stem: Is x² + 4 equal to (x + 2)²? Check by expanding.
questions.answer: No: (x + 2)² = x² + 4x + 4. x² + 4 cannot be factorised with real numbers.
questions.markingKey: No: (x + 2)² = x² + 4x + 4. x² + 4 cannot be factorised with real numbers.

questions.stem: Factorise 5x² − 20x.
Factorise x² − 49.
Factorise x² + 7x + 12.
Factorise ax + bx − ay − by.
questions.answer: x(a + b) − y(a + b) = (a + b)(x − y).
questions.markingKey: x(a + b) − y(a + b) = (a + b)(x − y).

questions.stem: Factorise 2x² − 18 completely, and hence find (2x² − 18) ÷ (x + 3).
Solve x + 7 = 12.
In one line: why must we do the same operation on both sides of an equation?
questions.answer: To keep the two sides equal (balance) — otherwise the equality no longer holds.
questions.markingKey: To keep the two sides equal (balance) — otherwise the equality no longer holds.

questions.stem: A student solves 3x = 12 as x = 12 − 3 = 9. Correct it and verify.
Solve 2x − 5 = 11.
Solve 3(x − 2) = 2x + 4.
Solve x/2 + x/3 = 10.
The sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 63. Find them.
A two-digit number has digits adding to 9. Reversing the digits gives a number 27 more than the original. Find the number and verify.
Write the formula for the area of a trapezium.
In one line: why is the area of a parallelogram base × height and not side × side?
questions.answer: Only the perpendicular height measures how 'tall' the shape is; the slanted side is longer than the height.
questions.markingKey: Only the perpendicular height measures how 'tall' the shape is; the slanted side is longer than the height.

questions.stem: Two rhombuses have the same side length but different areas. How is that possible?
questions.answer: Their angles differ, so their diagonals (and area = ½ d₁d₂) differ; a 'flatter' rhombus has less area.
questions.markingKey: Their angles differ, so their diagonals (and area = ½ d₁d₂) differ; a 'flatter' rhombus has less area.

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides 10 cm and 14 cm and height 6 cm. Find its area.
Find the area of a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm.
A field is a quadrilateral. One diagonal is 24 m and the perpendiculars from the other two vertices onto it are 8 m and 13 m. Find the area.
Write the formula for the circumference of a circle.
In one line: what does π represent?
questions.answer: The ratio of circumference to diameter, the same for every circle (≈ 3.14 or 22/7).
questions.markingKey: The ratio of circumference to diameter, the same for every circle (≈ 3.14 or 22/7).

questions.stem: If the radius is doubled, by what factor do the circumference and the area change?
Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm (π = 22/7).
The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Find its radius and area (π = 22/7).
Find the perimeter of a semicircle of diameter 14 cm (π = 22/7).
To find the area of an L-shaped figure, what is the first step?
questions.answer: Split it into rectangles (or subtract a rectangle from a larger one).
questions.markingKey: Split it into rectangles (or subtract a rectangle from a larger one).

questions.stem: In one line: why is the perimeter of an L-shape equal to the perimeter of the rectangle that just encloses it?
questions.answer: The two inner edges of the notch are exactly as long as the missing outer edges, so the total is unchanged.
questions.markingKey: The two inner edges of the notch are exactly as long as the missing outer edges, so the total is unchanged.

questions.stem: A student finds the area of two overlapping shapes by adding their areas. What is the error? Give a quick example.
questions.answer: The overlap is counted twice; e.g. two 2 × 2 squares overlapping in a 1 × 1 region cover 4 + 4 − 1 = 7, not 8.
questions.markingKey: The overlap is counted twice; e.g. two 2 × 2 squares overlapping in a 1 × 1 region cover 4 + 4 − 1 = 7, not 8.

questions.stem: A 10 cm × 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm × 3 cm rectangle cut from one corner. Find the remaining area.
From a square of side 14 cm, a quarter-circle of radius 7 cm is cut from one corner. Find the remaining area (π = 22/7).
A running track is a rectangle 100 m by 63 m with a semicircle on each 63 m end. Find the length of the track (π = 22/7).
questions.answer: Two straights 200 m + one full circle of diameter 63 m = 198 m → 398 m.
questions.markingKey: Two straights 200 m + one full circle of diameter 63 m = 198 m → 398 m.

questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 20 m × 15 m. A path 2 m wide runs inside along the boundary. Find the area of the path.
A circular table of diameter 1.4 m stands on a 3 m × 2 m rug. Find the visible area of the rug and the cost of cleaning it at ₹200/m².
Write the total surface area of a cube of edge a.
In one line: why is the curved surface area of a cylinder 2πrh?
questions.answer: Unrolling the curved surface gives a rectangle with length = circumference 2πr and width = height h.
questions.markingKey: Unrolling the curved surface gives a rectangle with length = circumference 2πr and width = height h.

questions.stem: If every edge of a cuboid is doubled, what happens to its volume and its surface area? Explain.
questions.answer: Volume × 8 (three dimensions doubled); surface area × 4 (each face's two dimensions doubled).
questions.markingKey: Volume × 8 (three dimensions doubled); surface area × 4 (each face's two dimensions doubled).

questions.stem: A cuboid measures 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm. Find its volume and total surface area.
Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (π = 22/7).
An open box (no lid) is 10 cm × 8 cm × 6 cm high. How much sheet metal is needed?
A room is 6 m × 5 m × 4 m high. Find the cost of painting the four walls and the ceiling at ₹20 per m².
A cylindrical tank has radius 1.4 m and height 2 m. Find its capacity in litres and the time to fill it at 100 L/min (π = 22/7).
